situations.situation: pursuing a stated goal or executing a plan

quotes.chongdae:run: The engine is `chongdae.py` at this plugin's root — the session-start line `chongdae: …` gives its full path
quotes.file:AGENTS.md: The installed release orchestrates changes, never this checkout's `plugin/chongdae.py` or the root shim.

findings.why: In this repository, 'this plugin's root' could be read as the checkout's own plugin/ directory or the root shim, both of which carry a chongdae.py. AGENTS.md forbids driving the run with either one. The skill already points to the path from the session-start line, and that path is the installed release.

class_quote.quote: The installed release orchestrates changes, never this checkout's `plugin/chongdae.py` or the root shim.

quotes.file:AGENTS.md: For behavior changes, run `python3 test_chongdae.py` from this repository root.
quotes.chongdae:run: Attach repeatable task checks with `--check` so the runner keeps their own exit and output.

findings.why: Both members ask for verification of a behavior change. AGENTS.md says to run the test suite directly, and the run skill says to attach repeatable checks to the task. If the suite is run as plain Bash, nothing about it gets recorded in the run.

class_quote.quote: Attach repeatable task checks with `--check` so the runner keeps their own exit and output.

situations.situation: asking what happened or what is open

quotes.dwitbuk:review: Use when the session-start line says objections are undisposed, when the person asks what happened or what is open, before a merge, or on a project whose lock has no `reviewer` role (there, run the review by hand).
quotes.jokbo:read: Use when a question about this project comes up that its records may already answer — "what did we decide about X", "why is it this way", "where is X described", "what happened in that run / today", "what changed since I last looked", "what stands on this file before I change it", or the owner asks any of these.

findings.why: Both claim the question "what happened". dwitbuk answers it by relaying review findings to the person and recording their dispositions. jokbo answers it by quoting the project's own records and commits. The two give different answers: one is a disposition workflow, the other a read-only quotation. Neither text says which one comes first or how one yields to the other. dwitbuk's path also records the person's decisions (`dispose ... --by`) and can commit a hand-run review, so choosing between them changes what gets written and decided.

quotes.dwitbuk:review: A review run by hand is a record like a run: commit `reviews/<id>.json`.
quotes.plugin:chongdae: Writes go through this run; `python3 "<this plugin>/chongdae.py" run` advances it.

findings.why: Before a merge, the review skill writes and commits a reviews/<id>.json record when it runs by hand (steps 1 and 3), and the eyes step adds contradictions to the latest review. chongdae's mode says every write goes through the active run, and with no run in progress it refuses writes until one starts. A hand-run review commit made outside a run is work no run claims. The next review would flag it as outside-run, or chongdae would refuse it. A commit is hard to undo, so a person has to decide whether the review record gets committed inside a chongdae run or is exempt from that rule.

quotes.dwitbuk:review: What is still open is the session-start line (the hook prints it); `follow` lists the same by hand.
quotes.plugin:dwitbuk: `dwitbuk.py follow --target .` lists them, `dispose <review>/<n> --as accepted|dismissed --why ... --by NAME` answers one.

findings.why: The mode and the skill both report the open objections and name the same follow/dispose commands. The skill says the session-start line and `follow` give the same result.

class_quote.quote: What is still open is the session-start line (the hook prints it); `follow` lists the same by hand.

situations.situation: a decision waiting on the person

quotes.chongdae:run: Never write the owner's name on your own judgment, and never `--delegated` one the person did not hand off; the gates (`confirm`, `accept`) still need the person's `--by` or their delegation.
quotes.dwitbuk:review: If no person reads a finding and you dispose it yourself, say so: `--as ... --delegated "<why it was handed off>"` — recorded as a delegation, like a gate

findings.why: While a decision waits on the person, dwitbuk lets the session dispose of a finding itself with --delegated when no person reads it. chongdae forbids --delegated on any judgment the person did not hand off. The two disagree on whether the session may settle a person's decision without being handed it.

proposed.accept: dispose a dwitbuk finding with --delegated only when the person handed it off (a chongdae `delegate` D-id or their recorded words); otherwise leave it undisposed and ask the person

quotes.chongdae:run: Never write the owner's name on your own judgment, and never `--delegated` one the person did not hand off; the gates (`confirm`, `accept`) still need the person's `--by` or their delegation.
quotes.mangsang:operate: declare after the person approves, `--by <their name> --approved-in source:<the turn where they said yes>` (kept as a source first); without such a turn, sign `--delegated`.

findings.why: When the person has not yet approved a concept, mangsang falls back to signing --delegated. chongdae forbids --delegated on anything the person did not hand off. While a decision waits on the person, the two disagree on whether the session may sign in their place.

proposed.accept: sign a mangsang declaration or confirm --delegated only when the person handed it off (a chongdae `delegate` D-id or their recorded words); otherwise wait for the person's approval

quotes.chongdae:run: The lock's `reviewer` role ran as the run ended (its line is in the output; what it wrote went into the close commit) — you do not run a review yourself; what its findings need from a person, the reviewer says at the next session start.
quotes.dwitbuk:review: When the lock declares dwitbuk as chongdae's `reviewer`, the review already ran when each run ended — do not run another for the same run; go to step 2 with the latest `reviews/<id>.json` (`follow` lists what is open).

findings.why: Both cover the review findings that wait on the person after a run. dwitbuk's own text says the reviewer already ran at close and that the session should go straight to relaying the findings for disposition.

class_quote.quote: When the lock declares dwitbuk as chongdae's `reviewer`, the review already ran when each run ended — do not run another for the same run; go to step 2 with the latest `reviews/<id>.json` (`follow` lists what is open).

quotes.mangsang:operate: Show the list to the person; `confirm proposals.json --by <name>` on their word, or `--delegated "<why>"`
quotes.chongdae:run: Writes to the project need a run in progress (the PreToolUse hook refuses them otherwise).

findings.why: mangsang writes its confirm records into the project once the person decides. chongdae assumes every write to the project goes through a run. chongdae's text says how another product's records fit: as a task scoped to them.

class_quote.quote: A task whose work is another product's records (`hunsu lock`, a mangsang confirm) names them in its `--scope` (`--scope hunsu.json hunsu.lock.json`, `--scope mangsang`): inside its own scope they count as its work, and `run` prints their commit lines.

quotes.dwitbuk:review: For each they answer, `dispose <review>/<n> --as accepted|dismissed --why "<their words>" --by <name>`.
quotes.chongdae:run: Writes to the project need a run in progress (the PreToolUse hook refuses them otherwise).

findings.why: Recording the person's disposition writes dwitbuk's review record into the project, often after a run has closed. chongdae assumes project writes happen inside a run. Neither text says whether a disposition needs a run or a scoped task, or stands outside one.

proposed.accept: record a disposition inside a session run task scoped to dwitbuk's review records when no run is open, or let the person decide that dispositions stand outside runs

situations.situation: asking what was decided, why, or what stands on a file

quotes.jokbo:read: **Everything that stands on a file**: `file PATH` — the sections that speak of it with how current each is, who last changed it, and what each declared `file` read says.
quotes.mangsang:operate: Before editing a registered file: `lookup <path>` prints the confirmed relations standing on it — grouped by concept with its meaning, each with its quote, its confirmer and whether it is fresh now — and marks which ones the edit would make stale; read it instead of opening the record's JSON.

findings.why: Both members answer the question 'what stands on this file before I change it'. jokbo answers with `file PATH`. mangsang tells the agent to run `lookup <path>` and read that output instead. jokbo mentions 'declared `file` read[s]', but neither text says that mangsang's lookup is one of them, or which command should run first. So following one member may not give the same answer as following the other.

quotes.jokbo:read: **What was decided / where it is said / why it is so**: `find WORDS` — use the project's own words (a field name, a page name, a term from the plan).
quotes.mangsang:operate: `lookup R-xxxx` shows one relation, `lookup concept:NAME` what stands on a concept.

findings.why: For 'why is it this way' about a concept, jokbo's `find` reports what the declared decision reads (the net's questions and meanings) say. mangsang's `lookup concept:NAME` reads the same net directly. Neither text says which one to use or that they return the same thing.

quotes.plugin:chongdae: the run is the agent's container, so Edit/Write are refused until one starts

findings.why: When `check` fails with FAILED, mangsang:operate sends the agent to step 2, which writes a `proposals.json` and changes the net's records. The chongdae mode refuses Edit/Write until a run is in progress, so mangsang's repair assumes it can write files that chongdae only allows inside a run.

class_quote.quote: Writes go through this run; `python3 "<this plugin>/chongdae.py" run` advances it.

quotes.chongdae:run: start a FRESH subagent of this host with that prompt as its whole task (Claude Code: the Agent tool, general-purpose, run in the foreground; Codex: spawn_agent and wait); write the subagent's final JSON answer verbatim to the response path it names
quotes.hacheong:hire: A session dispatching its own subagent instead (a `native:` provider) runs the same argv with `--prompt-only`, gives the printed prompt to a fresh subagent, and writes its JSON answer verbatim to the response path.

findings.why: Both skills give the session the procedure for relaying a native: dispatch of a hacheong member (prompt-only argv, fresh subagent, verbatim answer to the response path). The steps are the same, so following either one gives the same relay.

class_quote.quote: A session dispatching its own subagent instead (a `native:` provider) runs the same argv with `--prompt-only`, gives the printed prompt to a fresh subagent, and writes its JSON answer verbatim to the response path.

quotes.chongdae:run: When a hired task stopped but its work is in the tree and you finish it (the sandbox could not run its tests; a guard read your own concurrent edits), `take <id> --why "..."` — never `drop`: a drop records done work as not done.
quotes.hacheong:hire: Never do a member's work yourself and never edit its answer.

findings.why: In some cases chongdae tells the session to finish a hired member's stopped build itself (take), or to take a small build itself instead of hiring. hacheong forbids the session from ever doing a member's work. While building a slice, the session cannot follow both.

quotes.mangsang:operate: After a slice: `register` the files the slice created first
quotes.plugin:chongdae: the run is the agent's container, so Edit/Write are refused until one starts
quotes.chongdae:run: Writes to the project need a run in progress (the PreToolUse hook refuses them otherwise).

findings.why: mangsang's after-slice step writes its record into the project (register, proposals.json, confirm). chongdae refuses writes when no run is open, and it counts files written outside a task's scope against other tasks. chongdae's skill already says how to fit mangsang's records into a run: a task that names them in its scope.

class_quote.quote: A task whose work is another product's records (`hunsu lock`, a mangsang confirm) names them in its `--scope` (`--scope hunsu.json hunsu.lock.json`, `--scope mangsang`): inside its own scope they count as its work, and `run` prints their commit lines.

situations.situation: reviewing, disputing or trying a change

quotes.hacheong:newbie: You do not open anything that person would not see (source files, tests, records) — if you learn how it works from the inside, you are no longer the person this role exists for.
quotes.hacheong:quibble: You do not read the tree — however the code happens to be, what the contract did not decide is not decided.
quotes.hacheong:nitpick: you do not read the implementation that may already exist, and you never read the builder's intentions
quotes.plugin:jokbo: at the first look at a file, a line per fact that bears on it

findings.why: These workers are useful only because they do not know the project's insides. Newbie sees only the README and the program, quibble sees only the contract, and nitpick never sees the implementation. jokbo injects a project map at session start and per-file facts at the first look at a file, which hands them that inside knowledge without being asked. Unlike chongdae and dwitbuk, jokbo's text has no clause that keeps it silent in a worker session. Each worker prompt also says it may run as a native subagent of the parent session, where any per-file hook would still fire.

quotes.plugin:chongdae: the run is the agent's container, so Edit/Write are refused until one starts
quotes.hacheong:nitpick: Do not commit, branch, or touch the run's record or the plan.

findings.why: nitpick has to write test files with Edit/Write and is told not to touch the run's record. chongdae's no-run branch refuses Edit/Write until the worker itself starts a run. If that branch reached a nitpick worker, the worker could not do its job without first starting a run, which it is forbidden to do.

class_quote.quote: Silent in a worker session (AGENT_WORKER=1): the run is the hiring session's.

quotes.dwitbuk:review: A review run by hand is a record like a run: commit `reviews/<id>.json`.
quotes.plugin:chongdae: the run is the agent's container, so Edit/Write are refused until one starts

findings.why: The skill's commit step assumes the session may commit a hand-run review's record with no run open. chongdae treats the run as the container for all of the agent's changes. A commit made outside a run is the same kind of work dwitbuk itself reports as `outside-run`. Neither text says whether this commit needs a run or a person's approval, and a commit is hard to undo.

proposed.accept: a person decides whether a hand-run review's record is committed inside a chongdae run or directly

situations.situation: setting up or adopting the project's agent environment

quotes.mangsang:operate: when a project first adopts mangsang
quotes.hunsu:compose: Calls to skills outside the lock are refused by hunsu's own PreToolUse hook.

findings.why: While the project's agent environment is being adopted, mangsang:operate's first-use procedure assumes its skill and engine can run. hunsu refuses any skill that is not in the lock, so mangsang cannot be adopted until hunsu:compose has declared and locked it.

class_quote.quote: If the user wants such a skill, that is a manifest change: `hunsu add`, then lock again.

quotes.plugin:chongdae: the run is the agent's container, so Edit/Write are refused until one starts
quotes.hunsu:compose: Write what they chose and run step 1 again.

findings.why: Both hunsu:compose (hunsu.json, hunsu.local.json) and mangsang:operate's adoption (mangsang/people.json, proposals.json) tell the agent to write files in the project. chongdae's standing mode refuses Edit/Write when no run is in progress.

class_quote.quote: the run is the agent's container, so Edit/Write are refused until one starts
